title: In a spectral space the generalizations of a quasi-compact set form an intersection of quasi-compact opens
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and let $E\subseteq X$ be a subset which is quasi-compact in the induced topology. Let $W=\{x\in X:\ \overline{\{x\}}\cap E\neq\emptyset\}$ be the set of points of $X$ that specialize to some point of $E$. Then $W$ is quasi-compact, and $W$ is the intersection of all quasi-compact open subsets $U\subseteq X$ with $E\subseteq U$; in particular $W$ is an intersection of quasi-compact open subsets of $X$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma 0A31 (label lemma-make-spectral-space, line 5005), implication (3) => (4) and the quasi-compactness of W shown in its proof (third paragraph); used in Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 0CAM (lemma-connected-topological, line 15071)
